questions.text: महाभारत के काल के दौरान धर्मशास्त्र और धर्मसूत्रों में निर्धारित सामाजिक व्यवहार संहिता के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following is a correct statement regarding the codes of social behaviour as laid down in Dharamasutras and Dharmashastras during the period of Mahabharata?

options.A: इन मानदंडों का पालन केवल ब्राह्मणों द्वारा किया जाता था।
options.B: इन मानदंडों का पालन सार्वभौमिक रूप से किया जा रहा था।
options.C: इन मानदंडों का पालन सार्वभौमिक रूप से नहीं किया गया ।
options.D: केवल शासक इन मानदंडों का पालन करते थे ।

options_english.A: These norms were to be followed by the Brahmins only.
options_english.B: These norms were being followed universally.
options_english.C: These norms were not followed universally.
options_english.D: Only the rulers followed these norms.

questions.solution: Option C is correct because the norms laid down in the Dharmasutras and Dharmashastras were not followed universally by all sections of society, as society was highly diverse and complex. Other options are incorrect as these norms were not restricted only to Brahmins or rulers, nor were they practiced uniformly across all regions and social groups.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किस राजवंश से रानी प्रभावती का संबंध था ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following dynasties did Queen Prabhavati belong to?
questions.solution: Option C is correct because Queen Prabhavati Gupta was a prominent ruler from the Vakataka dynasty. She was the daughter of the Gupta emperor Chandragupta II and married into the Vakataka royal family, later acting as regent.

questions.text: नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं, अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) । अभिकथन (A) : हड़प्पा एक सुनियोजित शहर था । कारण (R) : यहाँ सुनियोजित जल-निकासी प्रणाली थी ।
questions.text_english: Two statements are given below as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Assertion (A): Harappa was a well-planned city. Reason (R): It had a well-planned drainage system.

options.A: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं और (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।

options_english.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct reasoning of (A).
options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct reasoning of (A).
options_english.C: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
options_english.D: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct.

questions.solution: Option A is correct because the Harappan cities are famous for their grid-based town planning, and the advanced drainage system is one of the most significant pieces of evidence that confirms this planned nature of the city.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से हड़प्पा की वास्तुकला की विशिष्ट विशेषता क्या थी ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following was a distinctive feature of Harappan architecture?
questions.solution: Option C is correct. The use of standardized burnt bricks was a hallmark of Harappan architecture, enabling the construction of long-lasting structures and complex drainage networks, distinguishing it from contemporary civilizations that often used sun-dried bricks.

questions.text: स्तंभ-I का मिलान स्तंभ-II से कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:
questions.text_english: Match Column-I with Column-II and choose the correct option:
questions.image_description: Table containing Sanchi sculptures and their symbolic meanings.
questions.solution: Option C is correct based on the traditional interpretations of Sanchi iconography: 'Empty seat' represents Mahaparinibbana (i), 'Gajlakshmi' symbolizes good fortune (ii), 'Wheel' indicates the first sermon (iv), and 'Shalbhanjika' is associated with auspiciousness (iii).

questions.text: निम्नलिखित जानकारी की सहायता से भारतीय इतिहास के शासक की पहचान कीजिए : भोपाल शासक, 1868 से 1901 ई. तक शासन, सांची स्तूप के संरक्षण में सहायता
questions.text_english: Identify the ruler from Indian history with following information: Ruler of Bhopal, Ruled from 1868 to 1901 CE, Helped in preserving the Sanchi Stupa
questions.solution: Option B is correct. Shahjehan Begum was the ruler of Bhopal during that period and she is well-documented for her significant financial contributions and efforts toward the conservation and preservation of the Sanchi Stupa site.

questions.text: पाँचवीं शताब्दी के देवगढ़ मंदिर की यह दी गई मूर्ति निम्नलिखित में से किस देवता की है ?
questions.text_english: The given sculpture from the fifth century Devgarh temple depicts which of the following deities?
questions.solution: Option D is correct. The sculpture found at the Dashavatara temple in Deogarh specifically depicts the Anantashayana form of Lord Vishnu, where he is shown reclining on the serpent Shesha, which is a classic piece of Gupta-era iconography.

questions.text: वीरशैव अथवा लिंगायत परंपरा के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Virashaiva or Lingayat tradition?

options.A: वे ब्रह्म की सर्वोच्च सत्ता पर बल देते हैं।
options.B: वे मृत लोगों को नहीं दफनाते हैं।
options.C: उनका विश्वास है कि मृत्योपरांत भक्त शिव में विलीन हो जाता है।

options_english.A: They emphasize Brahman as the supreme entity.
options_english.B: They do not bury their dead persons.
options_english.C: They believe that on death they will be united with Shiva.
options_english.D: They are the followers of Vishnu.

questions.solution: Option C is correct. The Lingayat tradition, founded by Basavanna in the 12th century, emphasizes devotion to Shiva. A central belief is that after death, the devotee attains 'moksha' by merging with Shiva, which is why they do not practice traditional cremation but rather bury their dead.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित को कालक्रमानुसार व्यवस्थित कीजिए : I. तालीकोटा का युद्ध, II. नगलपुरम् की स्थापना, III. कमलपुरम् जलाशय की स्थापना, IV. गोलकुंडा की सल्तनत का उदय
questions.text_english: Arrange the following in chronological order: I. Battle of Talikota, II. Establishment of Nagalpuram, III. Formation of Kamalpuram Tank, IV. Emergence of the Sultanate of Golconda
questions.solution: Option C is the correct chronological sequence. Kamalpuram Tank formation (III) preceded the establishment of the royal suburb of Nagalpuram (II), followed by the emergence of the Deccan Sultanates like Golconda (IV), and finally, the decisive Battle of Talikota (I) in 1565 which led to the decline of Vijayanagara.

questions.text: स्तंभ-1 का मिलान स्तंभ-II से कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:
questions.text_english: Match Column-I with Column-II and choose the correct option:
questions.solution: Option C is correct. Brihadeswara Temple is in Tanjavur (a-4), Chennakeshava Temple is in Belur (b-3), Hazara Rama Temple is in Vijayanagara (c-1), and Chidambaram Temple is located in Tamil Nadu (d-2).

questions.text: निम्नलिखित जानकारी की सहायता से सोलहवीं शताब्दी के भारत के शासक की पहचान कीजिए: उसने चौदह बार अजमेर की तीर्थयात्रा की। उसने अजमेर शरीफ़ से नयी जीत के लिए और पुत्रों के जन्म का आशीर्वाद माँगा ।
questions.text_english: Identify the ruler of India from the sixteenth century with the following information: He went on a pilgrimage to Ajmer fourteen times. He sought blessings for new conquests and the birth of sons from Ajmer Sharif.
questions.solution: Option C is correct. Emperor Akbar was a frequent visitor to the shrine of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti at Ajmer. His devotion and his visits, particularly to seek blessings for heirs and military successes, are well-documented in Mughal chronicles.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसने गुरु तेग बहादुर जी की रचनाओं को गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब में सम्मिलित किया ?
questions.text_english: Who among the following included the composition of Guru Tegh Bahadur ji in the Guru Granth Sahib?
questions.solution: Option B is correct. Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru, included the compositions of his father, the ninth Guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur, into the final recension of the Guru Granth Sahib.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से मुगल भू-राजस्व प्रणाली के संदर्भ में कौन सा कथन सही है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following statements is true regarding the land revenue system of the Mughals?

options.A: राजस्व संग्रहकर्ता भूमि का कर केवल नकद में वसूलते थे ।
options.B: खेती की गई भूमि पर बिना किसी माप के कर लगाया जाता था ।
options.C: भूमि से प्राप्त राजस्व साम्राज्य का आर्थिक आधार था ।
options.D: कर संग्रहकर्ता साहूकारों की सहायता से लोगों से कर वसूलते थे ।

options_english.A: The revenue collectors collected tax of land in cash only.
options_english.B: The cultivated lands were taxed without any measurement.
options_english.C: Revenue from the land was the economic mainstay of the empire.
options_english.D: The tax collectors used to collect taxes with the help of Sahukars.

questions.solution: Option C is correct. Agricultural land revenue formed the primary source of income for the Mughal state, acting as the economic backbone that sustained the empire's administrative and military machinery.

questions.text: मुगल राज्य के कृषि समाज में महिलाओं की भूमिका के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से सही कथन की पहचान कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Identify the correct statement from the following regarding the role of women in agrarian society of the Mughal State.

options.A: महिलाएँ केवल कारीगरी का काम करती थीं ।
options.B: महिलाएँ खेतों में पुरुषों के साथ मिलकर काम करती थीं ।
options.C: तलाक़शुदा महिलाओं को दोबारा शादी की इजाज़त नहीं थी ।
options.D: महिलाएँ सभी क्षेत्रों में पूरी तरह स्वतंत्र थीं।

options_english.A: Only artisanal work were done by women.
options_english.B: Women worked in the fields with men.
options_english.C: Remarriage were not allowed for divorced women.

questions.solution: Option B is correct. In the Mughal agrarian economy, women performed a wide variety of essential tasks in the fields alongside men, such as sowing, weeding, and threshing, playing a crucial role in agricultural production.
questions.topic: Role of Women in Agrarian Society

questions.text: 1857 के विद्रोह के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से विषम की पहचान कीजिए : (A) आरा : कुँवर सिंह, (B) बड़ौत : शाहमल, (C) सिंहभूम : गोनू, (D) हैदराबाद : मौलवी अहमदुल्लाह शाह
questions.text_english: Find the odd one out regarding the revolt of 1857 from the following: (A) Arrah: Kunwar Singh, (B) Barout: Shah Mal, (C) Singhbhum: Gonu, (D) Hyderabad: Maulavi Ahmadullah Shah
questions.solution: Option D is the correct answer. While Kunwar Singh (Arrah), Shah Mal (Barout), and Gonu (Singhbhum) were local leaders of the 1857 rebellion, Maulavi Ahmadullah Shah was primarily associated with the uprising in Faizabad (Awadh), not Hyderabad.

questions.text: 1857 का विद्रोह भारत में _______ वंश के अंत का प्रतीक था ।
questions.text_english: The Revolt of 1857 marked the end of the _______ dynasty in India.
questions.solution: The correct fill is Mughal. The revolt of 1857 led to the formal deposition of Bahadur Shah Zafar, marking the final end of the Mughal Empire in India.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन जमींदारों पर इस्तमरारी बंदोबस्त के प्रभाव का सबसे अच्छा वर्णन है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following statements best describes the effect of the Permanent Settlement on zamindars?

options.B: उन सबको जोतदारों ने प्रतिस्थापित किया ।
options.C: उन्होंने अपनी भूमि ब्रिटिश को बेची ।
options.D: उन्हें भूमि पर महत्त्वपूर्ण नियंत्रण मिला ।

options_english.B: They all were replaced by Jotedars.
options_english.C: They sold their land to British.
options_english.D: They gained significant control over land.

questions.solution: Option D is correct. Under the Permanent Settlement (Istemrari Bandobast), the Zamindars were recognized as the legal owners of the land, giving them significant control over their estates, though they were also burdened with fixed revenue demands.

questions.text: संविधान सभा जनमत से किस प्रकार प्रभावित थी ?
questions.text_english: How was the Constituent Assembly influenced by public opinion?
questions.solution: Option D is correct. Public opinion influenced the Assembly as people voiced concerns outside the Parliament, through the press, and the members of the Constituent Assembly actively discussed issues with the public to understand their needs and expectations.

questions.text: नीचे दी गई जानकारी की सहायता से व्यक्ति की पहचान कीजिए: 1. वह संविधान सभा की सलाहकार समिति के अध्यक्ष थे । 2. वह पृथक निर्वाचिका के विरुद्ध थे । 3. वह स्वतंत्र भारत के पहले गृह मंत्री थे।
questions.text_english: Identify the person from the given information: 1. He was the head of Advisory Committee of the Constituent Assembly. 2. He was against the separate electorate. 3. He was the first home minister of free India.
questions.solution: Option C is correct. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel held these roles; he played a crucial role in drafting the Constitution's fundamental rights provisions as head of the Advisory Committee and was the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of India.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसकी सलाह पर गांधीजी ने एक वर्ष तक ब्रिटिश भारत की यात्रा की जिससे कि राजनीति में प्रवेश करने से पहले वे इस भूमि और इसके लोगों को जान सकें ?
questions.text_english: On whose of the following advice Gandhiji spent a year in travelling around British India for getting to know the land and its people before entering into politics?
questions.solution: Option B is correct. Gopal Krishna Gokhale was Mahatma Gandhi's political mentor, and it was upon his advice that Gandhi spent his first year in India traveling across the country to observe the conditions of the people before immersing himself in active political life.
questions.chapter: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement

questions.text: गांधीजी ने 'रॉलेट एक्ट' के विरुद्ध देशव्यापी अभियान क्यों चलाया ? निम्नलिखित में से सर्वोपयुक्त विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english: Why did Gandhi call for a nationwide campaign against the 'Rowlatt Act'? Choose the appropriate option from the following:

options.A: ब्रिटिश सरकार ने सारे स्कूल और कॉलेजों को बंद कर दिया ।
options.C: ब्रिटिश सरकार ने बिना जाँच के कारावास की अनुमति दे दी थी।
options.D: लोग ब्रिटिश सरकार से स्वतंत्रता की अपेक्षा कर रहे थे ।

options_english.A: The British Government closed all the schools and colleges.
options_english.B: The first World War came to an end.
options_english.C: British Govt. permitted detention without trial.
options_english.D: People expected independence from the British.

questions.solution: Option C is correct. The Rowlatt Act of 1919 granted the British colonial government draconian powers to curb political activities and allowed for the detention of political prisoners without trial for up to two years, which Gandhi rightly perceived as an infringement of fundamental rights.
questions.chapter: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement

questions.text: (a) हड़प्पावासियों द्वारा मुहरों और मुद्रांकनों का प्रयोग लंबी दूरी के संपर्कों को सुविधाजनक बनाने के लिए क्यों होता था ? उदाहरणों सहित स्पष्ट कीजिए । अथवा (b) हड़प्पा के प्रशासन पर पुरातत्त्वविदों के विभिन्न विचार थे।इस कथन की व्याख्या उदाहरणों सहित कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: (a) Why were the seals and sealings used by the Harappans to facilitate long distance communication? Explain with examples. OR (b) There were different views of archaeologists on the administration of Harappa. Explain the statement with examples.

key_points: Seals were used to secure the contents of trade goods.
They acted as a sign of ownership during transit.
The impression of the seal (sealing) left on clay verified that the package remained untampered.

sub_questions.solution: Harappan seals were vital for long-distance trade. Traders used them to secure shipments of goods. By applying a clay sealing over a knot on a package, the sender ensured ownership. If the sealing reached the destination intact, the receiver knew the contents had not been tampered with, verifying authenticity.

questions.solution: The Harappan administration remains a subject of intense debate among archaeologists. Some scholars argue for a centralized authority, citing uniform urban planning, standard brick sizes, and trade practices across vast regions. Others suggest that the lack of royal burials or grand palaces implies a system of local governance, potentially dominated by powerful merchants or priests rather than a single autocratic ruler.

questions.text: मौर्य साम्राज्य को जानने के किन्हीं तीन स्रोतों की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Explain any three sources to know about Maurya Empire.

key_points: Archaeological finds like Ashokan inscriptions/pillars.
Literary sources like Arthashastra by Chanakya.
Accounts of foreign travelers like Megasthenes' Indica.

questions.solution: Three primary sources for the Maurya Empire include archaeological evidence like the rock and pillar inscriptions commissioned by Ashoka, which reveal his governance and ethics. Literary sources, most notably Kautilya's Arthashastra, provide detailed administrative guidance, while Megasthenes' Indica, an account by a Greek envoy, offers external perspectives on the Mauryan court and city life.

questions.text: (a) विजयनगर साम्राज्य में अमर-नायकों की भूमिका का विश्लेषण कीजिए । अथवा (b) विजयनगर साम्राज्य के शासकों द्वारा विजयनगर के स्थल को अपनी राजधानी के रूप में चुनने के कारकों का विश्लेषण कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: (a) Analyse the role of Amara-nayakas in the Vijayanagara empire. OR (b) Analyse the factors that led the rulers of the Vijayanagara empire to choose the site of Vijayanagara as their capital.

key_points: Military commanders who managed territories assigned by the king.
Collected taxes and maintained local order.
Provided military support and tribute to the central empire.

sub_questions.solution: Amara-nayakas were military commanders in the Vijayanagara Empire who functioned as regional administrators. They were assigned land, from which they collected revenue to maintain troops, perform administrative duties, and send a portion of this revenue as annual tribute to the central royal treasury.

questions.solution: The site of Vijayanagara was strategically chosen as the capital because of its natural defense mechanisms. It was located in the Tungabhadra river valley, surrounded by rocky terrain and hills that served as a natural fortification. Furthermore, the area held significant historical and religious importance as it was believed to be the kingdom of Vali and Sugriva from the Ramayana, enhancing the legitimacy of the rulers.

questions.text: मुगल काल में पंचायतों की भूमिका का वर्णन कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Describe the role of Panchayats in the Mughal era.

key_points: Settling disputes between villagers.
Managing common social and economic resources.
Ensuring revenue payment and social cohesion within the village.

questions.solution: In the Mughal era, village panchayats were the primary instruments of local self-governance. Composed of village elders, they settled disputes, enforced local customs, and managed common lands and water resources. Additionally, they played a vital role in ensuring that the village collectively paid the land revenue demanded by the state, thereby maintaining order and local social cohesion.

questions.text: भारतीय समाज के सुधार के लिए विलियम बैंटिंक द्वारा अपनाई गई नीतियों का विश्लेषण कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Analyse the policies adopted by William Bentinck to reform Indian society.

key_points: Abolition of Sati practice in 1829.
Suppression of Thuggee gangs.
Promotion of Western education and modern administrative reforms.

questions.solution: Governor-General William Bentinck introduced several reformist policies aimed at modernizing Indian society. His most notable social reform was the abolition of the practice of Sati in 1829. He also took decisive action to suppress the organized criminal gangs known as the Thuggees. Furthermore, he advocated for Western-style education and administrative transparency, laying foundations for systemic colonial governance.

questions.text: संविधान सभा की चर्चाओं के दौरान बी. आर. अम्बेडकर ने कहा था कि वह एक शक्तिशाली केन्द्र चाहते हैं जो 1935 के एक्ट के अधीन बनाए गए केन्द्र से कहीं अधिक शक्तिशाली हो । इस कथन की परख कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: During the debates in Constituent Assembly, B.R. Ambedkar told that he wanted a strong centre, much stronger than the centre we had created under the Act of 1935. Analyse the statement.

key_points: Focus on unity and integrity post-partition.
Need for state intervention during crises.
Preventing regional balkanization.

questions.solution: B.R. Ambedkar advocated for a strong centre to ensure national unity and integrity, especially in the volatile post-partition context. He believed that only a robust central government could manage the complex challenges of India, prevent potential fragmentation, and effectively coordinate development programs across diverse states. The 1935 Act framework was viewed as too decentralized for the needs of a newly independent nation.

questions.text: (a) प्राचीन भारतीय समाज में भूमि-अनुदान की प्रकृति और विशेषताओं की परख कीजिए । अथवा (b) छठी शताब्दी ई. पूर्व से कृषि उत्पादकता में वृद्धि के लिए अपनाई गई विभिन्न रणनीतियों की परख कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: (a) Examine the nature and characteristics of the land grants in ancient Indian society. OR (b) Examine the various strategies used to enhance agricultural output from the sixth BCE onwards.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) Nature and characteristics of land grants

key_points: Grants given to religious institutions and Brahmins.
Often recorded on copper plates.
Enabled kings to extend agriculture into new territories.
Led to social and administrative changes in the countryside.

sub_questions.solution: Land grants in ancient India, often documented on copper plates, were primarily made to Brahmanas and religious institutions. These grants served as a mechanism for kings to extend their influence into uncultivated areas, promote agricultural growth, and secure the loyalty of the elite Brahmana class. By granting land, rulers could delegate administrative responsibility, which in turn altered the socio-economic structure of rural society, often turning the grantees into local administrators or landlords over time, thereby increasing state revenue and legitimacy.

questions.solution: Agricultural productivity improved significantly from the sixth century BCE onwards through several strategic changes. First, the introduction of the iron-tipped ploughshare allowed for the cultivation of heavier, alluvial soils. Second, the expansion of irrigation through tanks, wells, and canals ensured a more reliable water supply, particularly in arid areas. Third, the transition to transplanting paddy in parts of the Ganga valley allowed for much denser and more successful crop yields. These technological and procedural advancements collectively laid the foundation for the surplus production that enabled the growth of complex state systems and urbanization during the period.

questions.text: (a) 'फ्रांसिस बर्नियर ने भारत में जो कुछ देखा, उसकी तुलना यूरोप से की।' इस कथन की व्याख्या उदाहरणों सहित कीजिए । अथवा (b) 'इब्न बतूता ने भारत में अपने अनुभवों पर विस्तृत रूप से लिखा है।' इस कथन की व्याख्या उदाहरणों सहित कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: (a) 'Francois Bernier contrasted what he saw in India with the situation in Europe.' Explain the statement with examples. OR (b) 'Ibn-Battuta has written extensively about his experience in India.' Explain the statement with examples.

sub_questions.text: (a) फ्रांसिस बर्नियर के यूरोप और भारत की तुलना
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Bernier's comparison of Europe and India

key_points: Critique of the absence of private property in land.
Comparison of the pauperized state of peasants versus European farmers.
Observations on cities as 'camp towns' supported by the royal court.

sub_questions.solution: Francois Bernier, a French physician and traveler, consistently compared Indian conditions unfavorably with Europe. He was particularly critical of the absence of private property in land in Mughal India, arguing that it led to poor agricultural management and oppressed peasants compared to his native France. He described Indian cities as mere 'camp towns' that owed their existence solely to the royal court, contrasting them with the more autonomous and stable urban centers of Europe. His observations reflected a colonial-era bias that painted the Mughal system as economically stagnant and despotic.

questions.solution: Ibn-Battuta’s account, the 'Rihla', provides a remarkably detailed and observant record of his travels in 14th-century India. He extensively documented the unique socio-cultural practices he encountered, such as the elaborate postal system (Uluq and Dawa), the sophisticated market networks, and the functioning of the Sultanate under Muhammad bin Tughlaq. His writing captures the diversity of the Indian subcontinent, describing everything from exotic fruits and local culinary habits to complex religious rituals and administrative governance. His work stands as an invaluable primary source for understanding the lived experiences and administrative realities of the Delhi Sultanate period.

questions.text: (a) कल्पना कीजिए कि आप एक ऐतिहासिक शोध दल का नेतृत्व कर रहे हैं। आप ग्रामीण ग्रस्तता को बढ़ावा देने में रैयतवाड़ी प्रणाली की भूमिका और बंबई-दक्कन के किसानों पर इसके दीर्घकालिक परिणामों की व्याख्या कैसे करेंगे ? स्पष्ट कीजिए । अथवा (b) आपको एक रिपोर्ट तैयार करने के लिए कहा गया है कि अमेरिकी गृहयुद्ध के अंत ने भारत के दक्कन में कपास की उछाल को कैसे प्रभावित किया। आप इन परिवर्तनों का आकलन कैसे करेंगे, स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: (a) Imagine you are leading a historical research team. How would you explain the role of Ryotwari System in fostering rural indebtness and its long-term consequences on Bombay-Deccan peasantry? OR (b) You are asked to prepare a report on how the end of the American Civil War affected the cotton boom in the Indian Deccan. How would you assess the changes? Explain.

key_points: Direct collection of revenue from peasants.
Inflexible revenue demand regardless of harvest outcomes.
Forced borrowing from moneylenders leading to debt cycles.

sub_questions.solution: As the head of a research team, I would evaluate the Ryotwari system as a major factor in rural indebtedness. Unlike previous systems, it extracted revenue directly from the individual peasant. When revenue demands were set too high and remained inflexible despite poor monsoons or failing harvests, peasants were forced to borrow from local moneylenders to meet the payments. Over time, these debts accumulated, leading to land alienation and long-term impoverishment for the Bombay-Deccan peasantry, as they became permanently trapped in a cycle of debt to save their ancestral lands.

questions.solution: The American Civil War had a profound impact on the Indian cotton trade. During the war, British mills faced an acute shortage of American cotton, leading them to look toward India, which resulted in a massive boom in Deccan cotton prices. Many Indian farmers and moneylenders invested heavily, encouraged by the sudden prosperity. However, the end of the Civil War caused the global market to flood with American cotton again, leading to a sudden, catastrophic collapse in prices. This ruined those who had taken large loans during the boom, leading to a severe agrarian crisis and debt-driven rural unrest in the Deccan region.

questions.text:
उपनिषद की कुछ पंक्तियाँ

यहाँ पर संस्कृत भाषा में रचित लगभग छठी सदी ईसा पूर्व के छांदोग्य उपनिषद से दो श्लोक दिए गए हैं :

आत्मा की प्रकृति

मेरी यह आत्मा धान या यव या सरसों या बाजरे के बीज की गिरी से भी छोटी है। मन के अंदर छुपी मेरी यह आत्मा पृथ्वी से भी विशाल, क्षितिज से भी विस्तृत, स्वर्ग से भी बड़ी है और इन सभी लोकों से भी बड़ी है

सच्चा यज्ञ

यह (पवन) जो बह रहा है, निश्चय ही एक यज्ञ है..... बहते बहते यह सबको पवित्र करता है; इसलिए यह वास्तव में यज्ञ है
questions.text_english:
Verses from the Upanishads

Here are two verses from the Chhandogya Upanishad, a text composed in Sanskrit c. sixth century BCE:

The Nature of the Self

This self of mine within the heart, is smaller than paddy or barley or mustard or millet or the kernel of a seed of millet. This self of mine within the heart is greater than the earth, greater than the intermediate space, greater than heaven, greater than these worlds.

The True Sacrifice

This one (the wind) that blows, this is surely a sacrifice While moving, it sanctifies all this; therefore it is indeed a sacrifice.

sub_questions.text: इन श्लोकों के मुख्य विषय का उल्लेख कीजिए
sub_questions.text_english: Mention the main theme of the verse.

key_points: Nature of the individual self (Atman) and philosophical definitions of true sacrifice.

sub_questions.solution: The main theme of these verses is the philosophical inquiry into the nature of the individual self (Atman), which is depicted as both infinitesimally small and universally vast, and the redefinition of sacrifice as an inherent natural process rather than just ritual.

sub_questions.text: इन श्लोकों के संदर्भ में आत्मा और वायु के बीच के संबंध का उल्लेख कीजिए
sub_questions.text_english: Mention the relationship between the self and the wind in the context of these verses.

key_points: Both are omnipresent and sanctifying forces in the philosophical view.

sub_questions.solution: In these verses, both the self and the wind are portrayed as pervasive forces. Just as the wind moves through everything and sanctifies it, the self is portrayed as existing within everything, suggesting a deep, metaphysical unity between internal self-awareness and the outer natural world.

sub_questions.text: यह स्रोत उपनिषदों के दार्शनिक विचारों को किस प्रकार दर्शाता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: How does this source reflect the philosophical ideas of the Upanishads?

key_points: Shift from ritual to metaphysical inquiry.
Emphasis on unity of self (Atman) and the cosmos (Brahman).

sub_questions.solution: This source reflects the core shift of the Upanishadic philosophy from outward ritualistic sacrifice to inward metaphysical inquiry. By equating the natural movement of wind to a 'sacrifice' and describing the self as encompassing the entire cosmos, it highlights the Upanishadic focus on understanding the fundamental unity between the individual soul and the universal reality.

questions.text:
अमीर खुसरो और कौल

अमीर खुसरो (1253-1325) महान कवि, संगीतज्ञ तथा शेख निज़ामुद्दीन औलिया के अनुयायी थे। उन्होंने कौल (अरबी शब्द जिसका अर्थ है कहावत) का प्रचलन करके चिश्ती समा को एक विशिष्ट आकार दिया। कौल को कव्वाली के शुरू और आखिर में गाया जाता था। इसके बाद सूफी कविता का पाठ होता था जो फ़ारसी, हिंदवी अथवा उर्दू में होती थी और कभी-कभी इन तीनों ही भाषाओं के शब्द इसमें मौजूद होते थे । शेख निज़ामुद्दीन औलिया की दरगाह पर गाने वाले कव्वाल अपने गायन की शुरुआत कौल से करते हैं। आज उपमहाद्वीप की सभी दरगाहों पर कव्वाली गाई जाती है।
questions.text_english:
Amir Khusrau and the Qaul

Amir Khusrau (1253-1325), the great poet, musician and disciple of Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya, gave a unique form to the Chishti 'sama' by introducing the qaul (Arabic word meaning saying), a hymn sung at the opening or closing of qawwali. This was followed by sufi poetry in Persian, Hindavi or Urdu, and sometimes using words from all of these languages. Qawwals (those who sing these songs) at the shrine of Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya always start their recital with the qaul. Today qawwali is performed in shrines all over the subcontinent.

key_points: It serves as a medium for spiritual ecstasy and devotion.

sub_questions.solution: In Qawwali, Sufism finds a medium for spiritual ecstasy and the expression of mystical love. questions.text:
नमक सत्याग्रह क्यों ?

नमक विरोध का प्रतीक क्यों था ? इसके बारे में महात्मा गाँधी ने लिखा है : 

प्रतिदिन प्राप्त होने वाली सूचनाओं से पता चलता है कि कैसे अन्यायपूर्ण तरीके से नमक कर को तैयार किया गया है। बिना कर (जो कभी-कभी नमक के मूल्य का चौदह गुना तक होता था) अदा किए गए नमक के प्रयोग को रोकने के लिए सरकार उस नमक को, जिसे वह लाभ पर नहीं बेच पाती थी, नष्ट कर देती थी । अतः यह राष्ट्र की अत्यधिक महत्त्वपूर्ण आवश्यकता पर कर लगाती है; यह जनता को इसके उत्पादन से रोकती है और प्रकृति ने जिसे बिना किसी श्रम के उत्पादित किया है उसे नष्ट कर देती है। अतः किसी भी वजह से किसी चीज़ को स्वयं प्रयोग न कर पाने तथा अन्य को भी उसका प्रयोग न करने देने तथा ऐसे में उस चीज़ को नष्ट कर देने की इस अन्यायपूर्ण नीति को किसी भी विशेषण द्वारा नहीं बताया जा सकता है। विभिन्न स्रोतों से मैं भारत के सभी भागों में इस राष्ट्र संपति को बेलगाम ढंग से नष्ट किए जाने की कहानियाँ सुन रहा हूँ। टनों न सही पर कई मन नमक कोंकण तट पर नष्ट कर दिया गया बताया गया है। दाण्डी से भी इस तरह की बातें पता चली हैं। जहाँ कहीं भी ऐसे क्षेत्रों के आस-पास रहने वाले लोगों द्वारा अपने व्यक्तिगत प्रयोग हेतु प्राकृतिक नमक उठा ले जाने की संभावना दिखती है वहाँ तुरंत अधिकारी नियुक्त कर दिए जाते हैं जिनका एकमात्र कार्य विनाश करना होता है। इस प्रकार बहुमूल्य राष्ट्रीय संपदा को राष्ट्रीय खर्चे से ही नष्ट किया जाता है और लोगों के मुँह से नमक छीन लिया जाता है। नमक एकाधिकार एक तरह से चौतरफा अभिशाप है। यह लोगों को बहुमूल्य सुलभ ग्राम उद्योग से वंचित करता है, प्रकृति द्वारा बहुतायत में उत्पादित संपदा का यह अतिशय विनाश करता है। इस विनाश का मतलब ही है और अधिक राष्ट्रीय खर्च। चौथा और इस मूर्खता का चरमोत्कर्ष भूखे लोगों से हज़ार प्रतिशत से अधिक की उगाही है। सामान्य जन की उदासीनता की वजह से ही लम्बे समय से यह कर अस्तित्व में बना रहा है। आज जनता पर्याप्त रूप से जग चुकी है अतः इस कर को समाप्त करना होगा। कितनी जल्दी इसे खत्म कर दिया जाएगा यह लोगों की क्षमता पर निर्भर करता है।
questions.text_english:
Why the Salt Satyagraha?

Why was salt the symbol of protest? This is what Mahatma Gandhi wrote: 

The volume of information being gained daily shows how wickedly the salt tax has been designed. In order to prevent the use of salt that has not paid the tax which is at times even fourteen times its value, the Government destroys the salt it cannot sell profitably. Thus it taxes the nation's vital necessity; it prevents the public from manufacturing it and destroys what nature manufactures without effort. No adjective is strong enough for characterizing this wicked dog-in-the-manger policy. From various sources, I hear tales of such wanton destruction of the nation's property in all parts of India. Maunds if not tons of salt are said to be destroyed on the Konkan coast. The same tale comes from Dandi. Wherever there is likelihood of natural salt being taken away by the people living in the neighbourhood of such areas for their personal use, salt officers are posted for the sole purpose of carrying on destruction. Thus valuable national property is destroyed at national expense and salt taken out of the mouths of the people. The salt monopoly is thus a fourfold curse. It deprives the people of a valuable easy village industry, involves wanton destruction of property that nature produces in abundance, the destruction itself means more national expenditure and fourthly, to crown this folly, an unheard of tax of more than 1,000 per cent is exacted from a starving people. This tax has remained so long because of the apathy of the general public. Now that it is sufficiently roused, the tax has to go. How soon it will be abolished depends upon the strength the people.
